result.summary:
Reviewed the actual diff (git diff main...HEAD), not just the handoff narrative.

1. OTP idiom / supervision (N/A, confirmed) -- diff is frontend-only: web/src/pages/dashboard/PlatformDashboardPage.tsx (new), web/src/router.tsx (+2 lines), web/src/pages/OidcCallbackPage.tsx (1 line changed), test/fixtures/uat/scenarios/platform/platform-login-routing-by-role.yaml. Zero files under lib/letflow/ or priv/repo/migrations/ touched -- no gen_statem, no GenServer, no supervision tree change to assess.

2. Scope creep -- NONE found. Implementation matches the approved design (lib/letflow/design/req369-platform-dashboard-page.md) section-by-section: component shape (default export, no props, Sec 1.1), imports exactly the contract list in Sec 1.2 (useAuth, useQuery, tenantsApi, queryKeys, QueryStateBoundary, classifyError/RendererState, Link, Navigate -- nothing extra), query shape matches Sec 1.3 exactly (queryKeys.admin.tenants({}), tenantsApi.list(), no new fetcher), self-gating predicate matches Sec 1.4 verbatim (Boolean(session?.roles.includes('PLATFORM_ADMIN')), redirect to /instances, both hooks called unconditionally before the gate -- confirmed by reading the file: useAuth() line 17, useQuery line 18-21, gate check line 23-27, i.e. hook-ordering constraint honored), heading is the fixed literal from Sec 1.5 with no tenant-context copy, quick-links nav has exactly the five Link entries with the exact to= values from Sec 1.6 -- no sixth link, no new route content. router.tsx change is addition-only (new import line + one new sibling route object). OidcCallbackPage.tsx change is exactly the one-line role-conditional navigate() from Sec 3's decision table, reusing the already-decoded payload.roles, placed at the same call site -- no other line touched. No new abstraction, behaviour, macro, or generic plumbing introduced anywhere; no premature framework machinery ahead of what this requirement needs.

3. Decision-record consistency -- consistent with docs/migration/decisions/0011-frontend-ownership.md (web/ is in Letflow's own scope, FRONTEND-DEV is the correct owner). No decision record contradicted; no framework/library choice made or second-guessed by this diff (reuses existing react-router-dom, @tanstack/react-query, existing tenantsApi/queryKeys/QueryStateBoundary/classifyError modules -- zero new dependencies).

4. Specific checks requested by the dispatch, verified directly against the diff/file (not the prior agents' claims):
   - router.tsx: `git diff main...HEAD -- web/src/router.tsx` shows only two added (+) lines (one import, one route); the pre-existing `{ index: true, element: <TenantDashboardPage /> }` and `{ path: 'dashboard', element: <TenantDashboardPage /> }` lines carry no '-' in the diff -- provably unchanged.
   - PlatformDashboardPage.tsx imports (read in full, lines 1-8): no `useTenantContext` import or call anywhere in the file -- only `useAuth` from `@/auth/AuthContext` is used for session data, matching the design's literal AC1 constraint.
   - Self-gating predicate: `Boolean(session?.roles.includes('PLATFORM_ADMIN'))`, matches design Sec 1.4/Sec 4 exactly, same as the TenantsPage.tsx/HealthDashboardPage.tsx precedent.
   - Query shape: `useQuery<TenantListResponse, ApiError>({ queryKey: queryKeys.admin.tenants({}), queryFn: () => tenantsApi.list() })` -- matches design Sec 1.3's table exactly (hook, queryKey, queryFn source, return/error types).
   - Role-conditional navigate table: `navigate(payload.roles.includes('PLATFORM_ADMIN') ? '/platform-dashboard' : '/', { replace: true })` -- matches design Sec 3's decision table exactly (PLATFORM_ADMIN -> /platform-dashboard, else -> / unchanged, both replace: true); both `window.location.replace('/')` fallback paths (invalid-token, callback-exception) are untouched in the diff.

No crutch, no broken/collapsed isolation (nothing to collapse -- frontend-only), no scope creep, no decision-record conflict. No non-blocking notes beyond what's already flagged as open questions in the design doc itself (Open Q1/Q2/Q4 -- none of these are implementation defects, they are pre-flagged design-time uncertainties already properly recorded, not new findings). PASS.
